text:
inc-bot: Pager: HIGH - Multi-GPU collective errors detected in prod-serving cluster (srv-prod-3). Triggered by multiple CUDA XID resets and NCCL rendezvous failures. Paging oncall: @oncall-jay

infra-bot: Automatic remediation started: draining affected pod group srv-infer-pt4-*. Attempting graceful restart policy. Logs attached to incident.

oncall-jay: I'm on it. Looking at recent deploys — anything rolled out in the last 15m? @ops_alyssa

ops_alyssa: No deploys. We had a burst of long sequences from a customer workload hitting TP4 pipeline. Seen spikes in seq_len and batchsize.

eng-ryan: I'm pulling GPU logs and NCCL traces. Preliminary: repeated "NCCL WARN Timeout" and then "CUDA error: unhandled XID 79" on GPU 2 and GPU 5. Several communicator resets.

ml-sophia: Customer impact: a handful of requests returned 502/timeout. Rate low but steady. We're seeing fallback to single-GPU variants for some routes (fallback policy fired).

oncall-jay: Can you paste the relevant kubectl logs?

eng-ryan: Sure — tail of dmesg from node srv-prod-3: ```
[12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.2: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, Channel: 00000002, pid: 42711, name: python
[12345.679012] ucg: nccl: WARN Call to ncclGroupStart timed out
[12345.679123] nccl: communicator reset, rank 2
```

ops_alyssa: Node shows occasional ECC correctable errors earlier today but nothing catastrophic. Network (IB) metrics show transient qdepth spike around the same time.

ml-sophia: Workload note: one customer route started sending long conversation contexts (>> typical) + forced large micro-batches. That would push mem + allreduce sizes.

oncall-jay: Triage plan: 1) Reduce pipeline micro-batch size globally for model v3.2 to avoid peak mem. 2) Force fallback to cpu/quantized variant for new requests for 10m. 3) Drain node srv-prod-3 and recreate with kernel driver restart. 4) Keep customers updated. Assigning tasks.

ops_alyssa: Taking step 1 and 2 now. Patching config: ``/configs/serving/exec_limits.json`` -> set "micro_batch_max": 4 for route /api/stream/v3.2. Applying via rollout patch to canary then global.

eng-ryan: I'll handle node drain + kernel restart. Planning: cordon srv-prod-3, drain pods (grace 30s), ssh + sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm; modprobe nvidia_uvm, restart containerd on node.

pm-lina: I'll draft a short customer-facing note in the status page: "Experiencing degradation on some multi-GPU workloads; mitigations in progress; some requests may use lower-capacity model variants temporarily."

infra-bot: Canary patch rolled to 2/10 pods. Observing CPU/GPU mem metrics.

eng-ryan: Drain started. Node shows 2 containers stuck in Terminating for >45s with `ncclAllReduce` in stack trace. Executing force kill on those containers.

ops_alyssa: Micro-batch cap applied cluster-wide. Immediate drop in GPU memory pressure on canary pods (~30% reduction). Good sign.

eng-ryan: Kernel module reload done. After restart, dmesg shows no new XID 79 on that node. Recreating pods now.

ml-sophia: Observability: per-route SLO errors reduced from 12% -> 3% on the canary after cap. However, still seeing rare cross-node rendezvous timeouts for some TP pipelines on remaining nodes.

oncall-jay: Any indication it's network fabric vs driver vs model?

eng-ryan: Logs show a small subset of NCCL rendezvous attempts failing with mismatch in participant list (one rank timed out waiting for rendezvous token). Could be ephemeral container restarts during allreduce causing mismatch.

ops_alyssa: I see a pattern where pods that were evicted/restarted by the drain wound up rejoining with different communicator ids briefly causing others to wait -> cascade.

ml-sophia: Short-term: enable per-request fallback to single-device execution for routes with seq_len>2048 and force KV cache reuse off for that window. That prevents huge allreduce sizes.

eng-ryan: Implementing quick guard: if seq_len>2048 -> route to model-quant-slim variant. Pushing config now.

infra-bot: Config push succeeded for traffic rule. Traffic routing change propagated to edge (0.8min).

pm-lina: Status update posted. Including note for enterprise customers that dedicated capacity unaffected.

oncall-jay: Monitoring for 20m. If rendezvous timeouts persist, we'll consider temporary cluster-level disable of TP pipeline for non-critical routes and shift to MP-only inference.

eng-ryan: After restarts + micro-batch cap + routing guard, error rate dropped to baseline. Still logging occasional nccl warn (1-2/hour) but not user-facing.

ops_alyssa: Marking node srv-prod-3 as stable, uncordoning. Will keep watch and add metric alert for XID spikes + NCCL timeouts.

ml-sophia: Follow-up action items: 1) Add guardrails in runtime to reject requests with very large seq_len unless capacity reserved. 2) Improve rendezvous robustness — ensure join-timeouts tolerate ephemeral restarts. 3) Add per-pod pre-stop hook to flush communicator cleanly. 4) Postmortem.

pm-lina: Filing incident ticket and scheduling postmortem meeting. I'll include customer impact timeline and mitigation actions.

oncall-jay: Thanks team. Reassigning alert to "resolved - monitoring". If we see any XID > 3 in 10m window, re-open pager. :white_check_mark:

inc-bot: Incident 3765432101 -> RESOLVED (mitigation: micro-batch cap + routing guard + node kernel reload). Root probable cause: bursty long-sequence traffic + ephemeral pod restarts causing NCCL rendezvous mismatches and GPU driver XID resets. Postmortem owners: @pm-lina, @eng-ryan, @ml-sophia.
